sections.h2: Where to record a deed in Huntingdon County
sections.html:
Deeds are recorded by the Huntingdon County Register & Recorder. The Register & Recorders Office covers three jobs: the Register of Wills, the Recorder of Deeds and the Clerk of the Orphans' Court.

Call (814) 643-2740 and choose option 2 for fee schedules, deeds, wills and marriage licenses. Recorded documents here run from 1787 to the present. Deeds, mortgages, satisfactions, releases, subdivision plans, agreements and easements, highway maps and secured transactions all live in this office.

A seller meets the office at the end of a sale, when the signed deed is recorded and the new owner enters the public index.

A UPI is the Uniform Parcel Identifier. Huntingdon County has required one on real estate documents since October 1, 2014 under county Ordinance 2014-2. It is the same number that appears as the tax parcel number on a tax bill and in the County Assessment Office.

The Assessment Department, through its Mapping Department, compares the document against county records and accepts or rejects it based on the accuracy of that number. The county says the check keeps recorded documents accurate and helps later real estate searches.

  • The UPI must be the first line on the document, below the top margin.
  • The top margin must be at least 2 inches.
  • The certification fee is $20 for each UPI number certified, paid with the other recording fees to the Recorder of Deeds.

A deed that covers a house and a separate lot can carry two parcel numbers, and each certified number adds $20 to the recording bill.

Walk-in customers take documents to the Mapping Department at 233 Penn Street, Huntingdon, PA 16652, between 8:30 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. on weekdays except holidays. A submission made after 4:15 p.m. is processed the next business day.

Mail-in and e-file customers send documents to the Recorder of Deeds, which processes them in the order received. The Mapping Department collects mail-in documents daily and returns them to the recorder within one business day.

The split affects timing. A closing agent who walks a deed in at 4:20 p.m. has missed the same-day window. A package submitted electronically goes through the recorder first and needs no trip to Penn Street. Ask the Register & Recorders Office which route fits your closing schedule.

The base recording fee for a deed or mortgage comes from the county fee schedule, and the office quotes it by phone at (814) 643-2740, option 2. One add-on is fixed: $20 per UPI number certified.

What to ask the office to total before closing
ChargeHow it is set
Base recording feeCounty fee schedule, quoted by phone
UPI certification$20 for each UPI number certified
Per-page chargeQuoted by the office
Realty transfer taxState rate of 1% of value, plus a local tax

Ask for the full total before closing, with the UPI line for each parcel. Whoever runs the closing sends these amounts with the deed, and the figures belong on the settlement statement.

Transfer tax is the larger cost. The Pennsylvania Department of Revenue sets the state rate at 1% of the value of the real estate. County recorders collect it, usually along with an additional local tax. Grantor and grantee are both liable, and the recorder passes the state's 1% along to the Department.

Some transfers are exempt, including certain transfers between family members, transfers to government units, deeds to burial sites, and property that passes by will or intestate succession.

sections.h2: Seller checklist before the deed is signed
sections.html:
Start with the parcel number. Check the latest tax bill, or ask the County Assessment Office, so the number typed on the first line of the deed matches the records the Mapping Department will compare it with.

  • Confirm the margin: at least 2 inches at the top of the first page, with the UPI number on the first line below it.
  • Decide how the deed will travel. In person it goes to the Mapping Department first. Mail and e-file documents go to the recorder, who passes them along for certification.
  • List every parcel being conveyed, because each UPI number certified is $20.
  • Ask the Register & Recorders Office for the total recording fee before the closing date.
  • If the transfer claims an exemption from realty transfer tax, ask the Department of Revenue or the closing attorney which paperwork supports it.

Subdivision plans are recorded in this office too. If you divided off a lot, check that the plan was recorded, because a deed that references a lot needs a recorded description to point to.

sections.h2: From signed deed to recorded deed
sections.html:
The path is short but unforgiving about details. The deed is signed and notarized at closing, and the closing agent confirms the parcel number against the tax bill. The UPI goes on the first line, with the top margin of at least 2 inches kept clear.

Next, the package is certified. In person, that means the Mapping Department before 4:15 p.m. if you want same-day service. By mail or e-file, the Recorder of Deeds receives it first and the Mapping Department collects it the same day, returning it within one business day.

Finally the recorder charges the fees, records the deed and adds the new owner to the index. If the number is wrong or the margin is short, the document is rejected, and you correct it and resubmit. A cash buyer and seller can close quickly, but the UPI step is the same for every sale, so build a day or two of slack into the schedule.

Military discharge records are recorded in the Recorder of Deeds office, but they are secure records closed to the public. A DD-214 is given only to the person named on it, who must show proper identification.

Anyone else asking for the information is directed to the county's military affairs officer at (814) 643-1360. If you need the document for a loan or a benefit tied to your sale, bring identification to the recorder's office in person.

Huntingdon County has an estimated 43,001 residents in 2025, down 2.4% from the April 2020 base, and 79.2% of homes are owner-occupied. The county has 21,148 housing units. The median value of an owner-occupied home is $183,200 for 2020 to 2024, and median gross rent is $810.

Most of the county is rural, and a Huntingdon County deed often describes land in more than one tax parcel. Each parcel needs its own UPI certification, so ask early what the deed and recording will cost.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Huntingdon County?
faqs.a: Record it with the Register & Recorders Office at (814) 643-2740, option 2. UPI certification for walk-ins happens at the Mapping Department, 233 Penn Street in Huntingdon.

faqs.q: How much is UPI certification in Huntingdon County?
faqs.a: It is $20 per UPI number certified. You pay it to the Recorder of Deeds with the other recording fees.

faqs.q: What is the cutoff for same-day UPI certification in Huntingdon County?
faqs.a: A walk-in submission to the Mapping Department after 4:15 p.m. is processed the next business day. Walk-in hours run 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays.

faqs.q: How far back do Huntingdon County recorded documents go?
faqs.a: Documents in the Recorder of Deeds office date from 1787 to the present day.

faqs.q: Who can get a military discharge record in Huntingdon County?
faqs.a: Only the person named on it, with proper identification. Others contact the county's military affairs officer at (814) 643-1360.
